audited_original_claim.statement: For lambda-partite perfect hypermatchings, k=sum_i lambda_i>=2 and m=min_i lambda_i>=1, D<=5184*max(2,k/m)*(2k-1)^10*s^10 under vertex-to-hyperedge queries.
audited_original_claim.locator: Repository product-permutation lift using final-journal Theorems 5.3/5.5 and Lemmas 3.3,3.5,3.6
audited_original_claim.proof_summary: Represent a hypermatching by independent permutations of the lambda_i*n vertices in each color class, grouping lambda_i consecutive positions per common block label. Lazy simultaneous assignment of a discovered hyperedge to a free common block label simulates each forward/inverse permutation query using at most one hyperedge query. Products of the source permutation pseudo-characters span the product degree filtration and induce product cubes of at least half their degree, giving degree<=2s^2 on the permutation product. There Delta<=2, beta_c>=1/3, M>=min_i(lambda_i*n), and total set-input size is k*n. Thus C<=72s^5 and D<=max(2,k/m)*C^2. Disjoint sensitive component transpositions form a multigraph on original hyperedges of maximum degree at most k; matching extraction gives s_product<=(2k-1)*s_hyper. Combine these inequalities.

assumptions: All lambda_i positive; n>=2; all lambda-partite perfect hypermatchings are allowed. Vertex queries reveal the entire hyperedge.
k=sum(lambda_i) and m=min(lambda_i) remain explicit parameters; uniform coefficients require controlling their growth.

audited_original_claim.notes: Repository derivation with full proof in docs/lambda-partite-lift.md, not a published priority or best-known claim and not independently reviewed. The alpha=1/2 witnessing argument applies to the product of permutation domains, not to the hypermatching domain itself. Therefore this does not establish a quadratic degree/sensitivity theorem for general hypermatchings.
